title: fleet-write: after the first live advisory_report, every later report answers HTTP 403, write-pace files it as an egress-proxy refusal (no back-off), and the relay hides GitHub's message, so the cause cannot be read
body:
domain:devx#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbWBtYWqaV8NhvUrShB

Filing gate: ① a defect in the PM relay tooling (`scripts/pm/fleet-write/**`, `scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs`), reach: measured on the live relay, 11 runs on 2026-11-02.
Business reason: the maintainer moved security findings to private advisories through the relay (#29178, #29222). On its first day the route took one report and refused every later one, from two sessions, and nobody can say why from the run logs. Security findings then fall back to session hand-delivery, which is the path the new route was built to replace, and the tooling keeps resending into the refusal.
Reader who acts: the `domain:skills` seat (owner of `scripts/pm/**` non-gate tooling, #29222's lane), with the maintainer for the one platform reading below.
Duplicate search: `is:issue advisory_report` → 2 hits (#29160, #29111, both closed, the cards that built the route); `is:issue isProxyRefusal` → 3 (#19774, #22452, #19822, unrelated); `is:issue security-advisories reports 403` → 5, none about this.
Maintainer word: 「排查一下，这个是技能的bug吗」 (Warren, project thread "Plan the release checklist run", 2026-11-02 14:06 UTC).

## What was measured

- Run 41455125597 (13:41Z): `advisory_report` → HTTP 201, an advisory id, state `triage`. The follow-up `advisory_collaborators_add` (run 41455906056) also landed.
- Every later `advisory_report`, from this session and from `session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk`, answered HTTP 403: runs 41455199874, 41455238314, 41455319128, 41455343428, 41455412342, 41455423232, 41455492312, 41455611641. The token step, the action version and the `permission-repository-advisories` input are identical in the 201 run and the 403 runs, so the refusal is GitHub's answer to the second and later reports, not the mint.

## Three defects in the tooling

1. **`write-pace` reads GitHub's 403 as the egress proxy's.** Each 403 run prints `write-pace: HTTP 403 was the egress PROXY refusing this request's path, not GitHub answering — a route refusal. No stop marker written, and the slot this write took is given back`. The relay runs on a GitHub Actions runner with no egress proxy, so that cannot be true there. `isProxyRefusal` returns true for any body whose `documentation_url` is not on `github.com`, and this endpoint's 403 evidently carries such a URL (or one the regex misses). Effect: no stop marker, no back-off, and sessions kept re-sending into the same refusal (8 refused strokes in 6 minutes).
2. **The relay hides the platform's reason.** For advisory rows the executor prints GitHub's `message` only when it is one of `ADVISORY_PLATFORM_MESSAGES` (six strings). The 403 row printed none, so the message is outside the list and the run gives no cause. A platform error message carries no advisory text, so it could be printed (length-capped) without breaking the "no summary, no description in the log" rule.
3. **The refused row tells the seat to "put this reading to the maintainer", but the reading has no cause in it.** Together with 2, a seat cannot tell a per-reporter limit from a missing permission from a duplicate rule.

## Expected

- `isProxyRefusal` is never true inside the relay runner (it is only meaningful in a cloud seat container), or it keys on the proxy's own message only; a GitHub 403 there takes the platform back-off path.
- An advisory row's refusal prints the platform's `message` and `documentation_url` (capped), never the payload.
- The skills seat then reads the actual reason once and records it in `references/rest-channel.md` (for example: a per-reporter or per-App limit on open private reports), with the seat-side rule that follows from it.

## Platform reading the maintainer can give in one look

Whether the advisory filed at 13:41Z shows in the repository's Security → Advisories with the App as reporter, and whether GitHub shows any limit on further private reports from that reporter.
